title: Training, fine-tuning, inference and RAG
summary: Make weight changes, retrieved context and generated output different paths.

claims.text: Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model. RAG supplies retrieved material to generation; retrieval is not the same operation as changing model weights.

levels.overview: Ask whether the need concerns fresh knowledge, behavior, or producing an answer.
levels.architecture: Draw a training-data/weights path separately from an index/query/context/answer path.
levels.detail: Inspect dataset versions, model identity, retrieval settings, evaluation scope and the allowed data.

example.input: A fictional policy changes while the model version stays fixed.
steps: Update the allowed retrieval source in the teaching scenario.
Compare which evidence is available to the answer.
Discuss separately whether a behavior change needs training.
example.output: A comparison of approaches, not a trained model or measured answer quality.
limits: No fine-tune, paid inference or model download is launched.

alternatives.label: Prompt and retrieval
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when source-grounded context addresses the requirement.

alternatives.label: Fine-tuning
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider a separately evaluated behavior/task adaptation need.

interview.question: When might you choose retrieval rather than fine-tuning, and when can both be useful?
answerHints: Define evaluation before making a selection.

instanceMappingPolicy: An explicit source-pinned link is required; names, icons and tags are not evidence.
